entry: City and metropolitan borough in the West Midlands, England (pop., 2025: 1.2 million). It is the largest local authority district in England by population and the second-largest city in Britain, commonly called the second city of the United Kingdom. Its urban area has 2.7 million people, and its wider metropolitan area 4.3 million. Birmingham was a medieval market town in Warwickshire that grew rapidly in the 18th century during the [[Industrial Revolution]]. By 1791 it was being hailed as "the first manufacturing town in the world," and its thousands of small workshops sustained a prosperous, highly skilled economy. Its political radicalism gave the city a pivotal role in British democracy. From 1940 to 1943 the German Luftwaffe bombed it heavily in the Birmingham Blitz, and later demolition and rebuilding led to extensive urban regeneration. The economy is now dominated by services. Its five universities make it the largest center of higher education in the country outside [[London]]. Birmingham hosted the 2022 Commonwealth Games.

City in north central [[Alabama]], United States (pop., 2024: 196,357). It is the third-most populous city in the state and the county seat of Jefferson County. Its metropolitan area, with over 1.19 million residents, is the largest in Alabama. Founded in 1871 during the [[Reconstruction era]], it grew from the merger of three smaller communities into an industrial center of mining, steel and railroads. It was named for Birmingham, England. Its rapid industrial growth from 1881 to 1920 earned it the nicknames "The Magic City" and "The Pittsburgh of the South."

Process of bearing or bringing forth offspring, also called parturition. In mammals, hormones cause the muscular walls of the [[Uterus|uterus]] to contract, expelling the [[Fetus|fetus]] when it is ready to feed and breathe. In humans the process is called [[Childbirth|childbirth]]. The mother's body is prepared by hormones from the pituitary gland, the ovary and the [[Placenta|placenta]]. The total gestation period is normally about 38 weeks from fertilization. Human labor has three stages, beginning with contractions and gradual dilation of the [[Cervix|cervix]] to 10 cm. After birth the umbilical cord is clamped and the newborn begins to breathe air. Offspring are either precocial, able to move almost immediately, or altricial, dependent on parenting. In [[Marsupial|marsupials]] the fetus is born at a very immature stage and develops further in its mother's pouch. Some reptiles, amphibians, fish and invertebrates also carry developing young inside their bodies.

Anniversary of a person's [[Birth|birth]], or of an institution's figurative birth. Birthdays are celebrated in many cultures, often with gifts, cards, parties or a rite of passage. Many religions celebrate the birth of their founders with holidays such as [[Christmas]], Mawlid and Buddha's Birthday. A birthday recurs each year, except that a February 29 birthday falls on another date in other years, unlike the birthdate, which is the complete date of a person's birth. In most legal systems a person reaches the age of majority on a birthday, usually between 12 and 21, though most countries set it at 18. In [[Canada]] and the [[United States]], a girl's 16th birthday is often marked by a "sweet sixteen" celebration. In some Hispanic countries the [[Quinceañera|quinceañera]] marks a girl's 15th birthday.

Small, flour-based baked food item, typically hard, flat and unleavened. Biscuits are usually sweet and may be made with [[Sugar|sugar]], chocolate, jam, [[Ginger|ginger]] or cinnamon. Savory biscuits are called crackers. Types include biscotti, digestive biscuits, shortbread and speculaas. The word derives from Old French *bescuit*, from [[Latin]] *bis* ("twice") and *coquere* ("to cook"), meaning *twice-cooked*, because biscuits were baked and then dried in a slow oven. Hard biscuits called hardtack were carried on long voyages, and the [[Royal Navy]] allowance at the time of the Spanish Armada in 1588 was one pound of biscuit plus one gallon of beer a day. In the United States and parts of Canada, sweet biscuits are called cookies, while the term biscuit denotes a quick bread.

Romantic or sexual attraction to more than one [[Gender|gender]]. The term originated in 19th-century sexology as a descriptor for people with both [[Homosexuality|homosexual]] and [[Heterosexuality|heterosexual]] attraction. Richard von Krafft-Ebing coined it in German in *Psychopathia Sexualis*, and Charles Gilbert Chaddock introduced it to English in an 1892 translation. Bisexual was reclaimed as a [[Sexual orientation|sexual orientation]] label in the 1960s and has since been defined in varied ways, including as attraction to men and women and as attraction regardless of gender. Scientists do not know the exact determinants of sexual orientation, but favor biologically based theories and do not regard it as a choice. U.S. surveys report bisexual identification at 4–5% of adults, rising to 15% among Gen Z. Some studies report elevated risks of mental health disorders among bisexual people, which may stem from minority stress. Bisexuality has been observed in human societies and elsewhere in the animal kingdom throughout recorded history.

Capital and largest city of [[Kyrgyzstan]] (pop., 2024: around 1,200,000). It lies near the border with [[Kazakhstan]]. The Khanate of Kokand built the fortress of Pishpek in 1825, and Russian forces destroyed it in 1860. A Russian settlement of the same name was established on the site in 1868. Renamed Frunze in 1926 after the Bolshevik military leader Mikhail Frunze, the city was renamed Bishkek in 1991, when the Kyrgyz parliament restored a modified form of the original name. It sits at about 800 meters (2,600 ft) on the northern fringe of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too Range, an extension of the [[Tian Shan]].

Chemical element with symbol Bi and atomic number 83. A brittle post-transition metal, bismuth resembles its lighter group 15 siblings, [[Arsenic|arsenic]] and [[Antimony|antimony]], in its chemistry. The free element is 86% as dense as [[Lead|lead]]. When freshly produced it is silvery-white, and surface oxidation gives it a rosy cast. It is the most diamagnetic element. Its only primordial [[Isotope|isotope]], bismuth-209, undergoes alpha decay with a half-life roughly a billion times longer than the age of the universe. Confused with [[Tin|tin]] and lead in early times, bismuth was shown by Claude François Geoffroy in 1753 to be distinct from them. Bismuth compounds account for about half of global production and are used in cosmetics, [[Pigment|pigments]] and pharmaceuticals, including bismuth subsalicylate, which can treat [[Diarrhea|diarrhea]]. Because its toxicity is unusually low for a heavy metal, bismuth alloys now meet needs formerly met by lead, which account for around a third of global bismuth production.

Large bovine with two living species. The [[American bison]] is found only in North America and is more numerous; it is more closely related to yaks and [[Cattle|cattle]] than to the true buffalo. Its two subspecies are the Plains bison and the wood bison. The [[European bison]], or wisent, is found in Europe and the Caucasus, where it was reintroduced after becoming extinct in the wild. American bison herds once numbered tens of millions on the Great Plains, but fell to fewer than 1,000 by the late 19th century. Conservation efforts, including reserves such as [[Yellowstone National Park]], have restored numbers to approximately 400,000, though most are commercially managed.

Peer-to-peer file-sharing protocol, first released in 2001 and developed by Rainberry, Inc. Users transfer files with a BitTorrent client, a practice called "torrenting." Trackers list available files and locate peers, called seeds, who can transfer them. Because there is no central server to limit bandwidth, downloads are considered faster than [[HTTP|HTTP]] and FTP. BitTorrent accounted for a third of all [[Internet|internet]] traffic in 2004, according to a study by Cachelogic. Its share has declined significantly since then.

Basic unit of information in [[Computing|computing]] and digital communication. The name is a portmanteau of *binary digit*, and its symbol is *bit* in IEC usage or lowercase *b* in IEEE usage. A bit represents one of two values, most commonly 1 and 0, though true/false and on/off are also used. Eight bits form a [[Byte|byte]], and four bits a nibble. In [[Information theory]], one bit is the [[Entropy (information theory)|entropy]] of a random binary variable with equal probability of 0 or 1, and is also known as a shannon after Claude E. Shannon. [[Data compression]] seeks a shorter representation of a string that requires fewer bits, while [[Error detection and correction]] adds redundant data so that errors can be detected or corrected.

First decentralized [[Cryptocurrency|cryptocurrency]] (abbreviation BTC). It was described in a white paper published in 2008 under the pseudonym [[Satoshi Nakamoto]], and its open-source implementation was released in 2009. Transactions are recorded on a public [[Blockchain|blockchain]] and validated through [[Cryptography|cryptography]], without central oversight. Consensus is maintained by proof-of-work mining, which consumes large quantities of electricity and has been criticized for its environmental impact. Its supply is capped at 21 million coins. From 2021 to 2025, El Salvador adopted bitcoin as legal tender before revoking it, and several countries have banned it.

Immensely viscous constituent of [[Petroleum|petroleum]], used mainly in road construction. Depending on its composition, it can be a sticky black liquid or an apparently solid mass. The word derives from Ancient Greek *ásphaltos*. About 70% of annual production is destined for road construction, where it binds aggregate such as [[Gravel|gravel]] into asphalt concrete. In American English the material is commonly called asphalt. Colloquially it is sometimes called [[Tar|tar]], though tar is not the same thing. Canada's [[Alberta]] holds most of the world's natural bitumen reserves, in the Athabasca oil sands.

Class of aquatic [[Mollusca|molluscs]] with a hinged pair of shells. Bivalves have laterally compressed soft bodies enclosed by two calcified valves joined by a flexible [[Ligament|ligament]] along a hinge line. They lack a head and a radula, and their [[Gill|gills]] have evolved into ctenidia used for feeding and breathing. Common examples include clams, [[Oyster|oysters]], cockles, mussels and [[Scallop|scallops]]. Most are filter feeders that bury themselves in sediment, where they are relatively safe from predation. Oysters were cultured in ponds by the Romans, and [[Pearl|pearl]] oysters are the most common source of natural pearls. Bivalves appear in the fossil record in the early [[Cambrian]], more than 500 million years ago. About 9,200 living species are known.

Icelandic singer, songwriter, composer and record producer. Born and raised in [[Reykjavík]], she began her music career at 11 and became known as lead singer of the [[Alternative rock|alternative rock]] band the Sugarcubes. Her solo albums, including *Debut* (1993), *Post* (1995) and *Homogenic* (1997), blended electronic, pop and avant-garde music. *Biophilia* (2011) was an interactive album with an accompanying [[IPad|iPad]] app. With sales of over 40 million records, she is one of the best-selling alternative artists of all time. She won the Best Actress award at the 2000 Cannes Film Festival for *Dancer in the Dark*.

American multinational investment company. Founded in 1988 as a risk management and fixed-income institutional asset manager, it is the world's largest asset manager and is headquartered in [[New York City]]. It manages the iShares group of exchange-traded funds and, with Fidelity, Vanguard and State Street, is one of the "Big Three" index fund managers. It has been criticized for investments in [[Fossil fuel|fossil fuels]] and in companies tied to the [[People's Liberation Army]]. BlackRock has sought to lead on environmental, social and governance (ESG) considerations; as of 2026, nine U.S. states had divested a total of $13.3 billion over its ESG policies.

Posthumous nickname of Elizabeth Short, American murder victim. Short, a native of [[Boston]], spent her early life in New England and [[Florida]] before moving to [[California]]. Her body was found in the Leimert Park neighborhood of [[Los Angeles]], and the murder, which involved mutilation and bisection, became one of the most famous unsolved crimes in U.S. history. The Los Angeles Police Department's investigation produced over 150 suspects but no arrests. The nickname may derive from the film noir *The Blue Dahlia* (1946). The case has inspired numerous books and films.

American pop-rap group formed in [[Los Angeles]]. It consists of rappers will.i.am, apl.de.ap and Taboo, with Fergie a member during its commercial peak in the 2000s. The group began as an alternative [[Hip-hop|hip-hop]] trio before the album *Elephunk* (2003), whose single "Where Is the Love?" (featuring [[Justin Timberlake|Justin Timberlake]]) topped charts in 13 countries. *The E.N.D.* (2009) yielded three Billboard Hot 100 number-one singles. The group has sold an estimated 80 million records and performed the [[Super Bowl|Super Bowl]] XLV halftime show in 2011.

Large forested mountain range in southwest [[Germany]]. The range lies in [[Baden-Württemberg|Baden-Württemberg]] and is bounded by the [[Rhine|Rhine]] Valley to the west and south. It is the source of the [[Danube]] and Neckar rivers and covers about 6,009 sq km. Its highest peak, the Feldberg, rises to 1,493 meters (4,898 ft). Historically known for forestry and mining of [[Ore|ore]] deposits, the area now depends mainly on tourism, which supports around 300,000 jobs.

Decentralized social movement against racism in the U.S. It highlights racism and police brutality against Black people.It began in 2013 as the [[Hashtag|hashtag]] #BlackLivesMatter, started by Alicia Garza, Patrisse Cullors and Ayọ Tometi after George Zimmerman was acquitted in the killing of Trayvon Martin. Protests followed the 2014 deaths of Michael Brown and Eric Garner. The 2020 demonstrations, after the killing of George Floyd by a [[Minneapolis]] police officer, drew an estimated 15 to 26 million participants. Most were peaceful, though protests from late May to early June escalated into riots and looting in most major cities. Support among American adults fell from 67% in 2020 to 45% in 2024.

British anthology television series. Created by Charlie Brooker, *Black Mirror* consists mostly of speculative fiction set in near-future dystopias, using technology and media to comment on social issues. The first two series aired on Channel 4 in 2011 and 2013, and later series aired on [[Netflix]]. It has 33 episodes in seven series, plus one special and the interactive film *Black Mirror: Bandersnatch* (2018). The series won the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Television Movie three times, for "San Junipero," "USS Callister" and *Bandersnatch*. Some reviewers count it among the best television series of the 2010s, while critics have found its morality themes formulaic.

Global [[Stock|stock]] market crash of October 19, 1987, also called Black Tuesday in some parts of the world. Worldwide losses were estimated at US$1.71 trillion, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 508 points, or 22.6%. Possible causes include fears that prices were overvalued, persistent U.S. trade and budget deficits, and the decline of the dollar. Portfolio insurance hedging may have accelerated the fall. Central banks in the United States, [[West Germany]] and Japan supplied liquidity, limiting the effect on the real economy, while the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's refusal to loosen monetary policy had longer-lasting consequences. The severity raised fears of a reprise of the [[Great Depression]].

American Marxist–Leninist and black power political and militant organization, 1966–1982. Founded in [[Oakland, California|Oakland, California]], by Huey P. Newton and Bobby Seale, it first drew attention for openly carrying firearms. It advocated decent housing, community control of education and police, and free breakfast for children. In 1969 [[J. Edgar Hoover]] called it "the greatest threat to the internal security of the country," and the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]] ran the covert counterintelligence program [[COINTELPRO]] against it. Its legacy is debated: older accounts called it more criminal than political, while historians Joshua Bloom and Waldo Martin call it one of the most influential black power organizations of the late 1960s.

English heavy metal band. Formed in [[Birmingham]] in 1968 by [[Ozzy Osbourne]], Tony Iommi, Geezer Butler and Bill Ward, the band adopted its name in 1969 and became known for [[Occult|occult]] themes, horror-inspired lyrics and down-tuned guitars. Their first three albums, *Black Sabbath* and *Paranoid* (both 1970) and *Master of Reality* (1971), are cited as pioneering heavy metal. Osbourne was fired in 1979 and replaced by [[Ronnie James Dio]], who recorded *Heaven and Hell* (1980). Iommi remained the band's core through many lineup changes. The band had sold over 70 million records as of 2013 and received two Grammy Awards for Best Metal Performance. It was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 2006. The original lineup reunited for a final show, *Back to the Beginning*, at Villa Park in 2025.

Marginal sea between Europe and Asia. It is bordered by Bulgaria, Georgia, Romania, Russia, Turkey and Ukraine, and covers 436,400 sq km (168,500 sq mi), excluding the [[Sea of Azov]]. Its maximum depth is 2,212 m (7,257 ft). Its water level has varied over geological time, and it was once an endorheic basin cut off from the world ocean. Major rivers, principally the [[Danube]], Dnieper and Dniester, supply it, so its drainage basin includes parts of 24 countries. Water flows out through the [[Bosporus]] and [[Dardanelles]] into the [[Aegean Sea]], while denser saline water below the surface is anoxic, which preserves ancient shipwrecks. Important ports include [[Istanbul]], [[Odesa]] and [[Sevastopol]].
